common_name: Amelia's Sand Verbena (Coastal Sand Plain Verbena)

planting.note: Sow papery, hard-coated achenes directly into loose, deep sand in full sun, since this species is a true sand-sheet specialist that fails in garden loam.

directions: Amelia's sand verbena is a low, sprawling wildflower found almost nowhere outside the deep sands of the South Texas Sand Sheet and Coastal Sand Plain around the King Ranch area, known from fewer than 100 locations across seven counties. It produces showy, fragrant pink-to-magenta flower clusters close to the ground from mid-spring into summer, a striking contrast against bare white sand. It demands loose, well-drained, nutrient-poor sand and full sun, and will rot quickly in richer or poorly drained garden soil. Because its range is so narrow, seed for cultivation should be sourced only from reputable native plant growers rather than wild populations.
